notes: WHY HE READ DEF 95, TERM BY TERM, BEFORE ANYTHING WAS TOUCHED. Dan Roundfield '83: 80 inches, drep 1.000 (1983 All-Defensive 1st team), BLK% 2.3 = the 0.8207 percentile of 1983, DBPM +0.5 = the 0.6196 percentile. recal_92's band runs p80 to p86, so _blk_evidence read 0.344, _paid_in_rim = 1.000 x 0.344 and the vote factor was 1 - 0.344 x (1 - 0.6196^3) = 0.738. PD2 = 0.55 + 0.45 x 0.9167 x 0.738 = 0.8544, card 85, smoothed to 83. d_score then reads him a BIG (d_bigness 1.0000) and takes 0.40 x perdef 83 + 0.40 x rimprot 87 + 0.17 x drb 91, raw 97.04 against a DEF_TOP of 104.25 - DEF 95, #1 of the 239 cards of 1983, above Bobby Jones '83 (94) and above his own '82 (94), the card recal_114 was written for.

THE FOURTEEN POINTS, MEASURED AND DECOMPOSED, not asserted. Running his own sheet through the rim chain twice - once with his ballot and once with drep = 0 - reads rimprot 88.4 against 74.1. Of that 0.1458 lift in band space, recal_53/92's voted CEILING (the channel _blk_evidence grades) contributes 0.0044; the remaining 0.1414 is recal_135's reinforcement line ID = ID + 0.25*(drep*hp), which is gated on nothing but height. So the meter was grading his payment by the one channel that paid him almost nothing. His '82 is the control: lift 0.1545 (92.0 against 76.9), a payment within a tenth of the same size, metered at 0.899 - and the weaker block line took the smaller deduction and printed four DEF points higher.

WHY THE SHIFT IS GATED ON THE BAND'S EDGE, AND THE TWO VARIANTS THAT MEASURED IT. Reading the band one width earlier for EVERY card is recal_162's form applied literally, and it reaches the subject identically (DEF 92) - but it also reaches BELOW recal_92's bar, where the file says there is no block evidence at all, and it breaks two anchors: Dennis Rodman '90 (79 in, blk p76, def 94 +-1) falls to 92 and Amen Thompson '24 (79 in, blk p80.2, def 94 +-1) to 91. The other direction - taking recal_135's height step down to 80 inches as a flat 1.0, which also reaches the subject - costs Scottie Pippen '97/'98/'99 fifteen to twenty perdef points each on block rates BELOW the bar, takes Paul George '17/'18 thirteen DEF points and breaks the Bulls '96 dial (r94). The landed form is the intersection: the earlier reading applies only ON the band's edge and above, where recal_135's channel already applies, and it still requires the blocks recal_92 asks for. 32 of 10,000 cards move.

WHY 80 INCHES IS NOT A FITTED NUMBER. It is drawn twice in this file already and both times as the same edge: recal_35's sweet band is FLAT at 1.0 from 75 to 80 inches, and recal_54's rep_hf is FLAT at its maximum 1.2 through 80. A card standing there collects the whole perimeter-vote premium the file can pay while being tall enough for the rim reinforcement to land on him in full - which is exactly the position recal_114's own subject stands in, and recal_114's receipt says so in its first paragraph ('6'8" EXACTLY - the top edge of recal_35's 6'3"-6'8" band'). recal_135 drew its height channel from the OUTSIDE of that edge because its own subject was 81 inches. This round draws the same edge from the inside.

ROUNDFIELD '80 AND '81 DO NOT MOVE, AND THAT IS THE FORMULA WORKING, NOT AN OMISSION. Their block percentiles are 0.9330 and 0.9235, both past BLK_FULL, so _blk_evidence already returned 1.000 for them before this round - the defect the ruling names never touched them. What holds them at DEF 95 and 94 is the OTHER half of recal_114's rule, the DBPM support: their percentiles are 0.832 and 0.732 against the subject's 0.620, so at VOTE_SUPPORT_POW 3 they keep 0.577 and 0.484 of the vote premium where he now keeps 0.238. Moving them would mean re-fitting recal_114's exponent, which is a different ruling.

NOBODY ROSE, AND NOTHING OUTSIDE perdef MOVED. The deduction still lands on the 0.45 vote premium and never on PD, so the within-season Pvot pool is bit-identical: 32 perdef cards moved and all 32 moved DOWN, 27 DEF and all 27 down, 16 OVR and all 16 down. rimprot moved on ZERO cards, every offensive attribute on ZERO cards, o_ovr on ZERO cards. The perdef top 12 is unchanged name for name.

THE CLASS THAT MOVED IS ONE ARCHETYPE. Every mover is a voted card at exactly 80 inches whose block rate sits at or near recal_92's bar: Dan Roundfield '82-'86, Shane Battier '03-'11, Scottie Pippen '89-'92, Kermit Washington '80/'81, Al Horford '18/'20, Scottie Barnes '25, Lonnie Shelton '80, Buck Williams '84/'85. Six-foot-eight forwards with All-Defensive votes, real but ordinary rim deterrence, and a d_score that grades them on the big vector.

THE HARNESS BROKE ON ONE CARD, AND IT IS WORTH RECORDING WHY. Exactly one card crossed the harness's ovr>=55 line - Shane Battier '12, 55 -> 54, pool 6,370 -> 6,369 - and because the pool is drawn by index every one of the 200 matchups is a different five afterwards. Both crash rows broke on the ORACLE edge. crash def glass re-ratified .38 -> .20 (feasible .0735 to .3355, true midpoint by r126's rule). crash off glass HAS NO SHIPPABLE TAX on this pool: the oracle reads +0.4996 AT ZERO TAX, four ten-thousandths under the +0.500 floor, and the whole feasible interval is negative (-0.52 to about -0.0017), so recal_167's 'midpoint of the POSITIVE half' rule has a single point to choose from and that point is not a tax at all. The row was therefore ratified on its OTHER harness constant - the law names 'the taxes AND SLOPES the harness ratified' in one sentence - with the tax HELD at main's 0.08 and the offensive-glass slope 0.26 -> 0.29 by recal_92's 'smallest move that clears both edges' (the window is one-sided; the blind read saturates near -0.756 against the -2.5 clamp and never approaches -1.5). It carries 0.0085 of oracle room where main itself carried 0.0063. All nine rows pass. FOR THE NEXT ROUND: main's crash-off tax has been pinned at the bottom of its range for three sweeps running (r167 recorded the same thing), so any round that thins this pool again will find the same wall.

THE METER IS NOW COMPLETE FOR HEIGHT AND FOR THE CEILING, BUT IT IS STILL BLIND BELOW THE BAND. A 79-inch voted card whose rim protection the ballot genuinely lifts - Dennis Rodman '90 is the measured example, 15.8 card points of lift on a block rate at the 76th percentile - is still metered at 0.000, and his recal_57 anchor is what stops this round from reaching him. If a later ruling wants that class, it is a ruling about recal_57's pin, not about this meter.
